words.enDefinition: a student who starts or runs a business venture while studying

examples.en: As a student entrepreneur, Maya tested her bicycle service between afternoon lectures each week.
examples.zh: 作为「学生创业者」，玛雅每周利用下午课间测试自己的自行车服务。

examples.en: The student entrepreneur talked about running a small design business while completing her degree.
examples.zh: 那位「学生创业者」讲了自己一边读学位一边经营小型设计公司的经历。

words.enDefinition: a business or social enterprise project led by students

examples.en: The university offered meeting space to a student-led venture selling repaired bicycles near campus.
examples.zh: 学校把会议场地提供给一个卖翻修自行车的「学生主导的创业项目」。

examples.en: Our student-led venture started in a design seminar and continued after the module ended.
examples.zh: 我们的「学生主导的创业项目」始于一门设计研讨课，课程结束后仍在继续。

words.enDefinition: a business owned by one or more students

examples.en: We bought our society's posters from a student-owned business near the main library.
examples.zh: 我们从主图书馆附近的一家「学生所有的企业」订了社团海报。

examples.en: The student-owned business hired two classmates to help with orders during the busy season.
examples.zh: 那家「学生所有的企业」在旺季雇了两名同学帮忙处理订单。

words.enDefinition: a company formed to develop or sell a technology or discovery originating at a university

examples.en: A university spinout demonstrated its new water sensor at the careers fair last week.
examples.zh: 上周招聘会上，一家「大学成果衍生企业」演示了新研发的水质传感器。

examples.en: The research team formed a university spinout to develop the software beyond the grant period.
examples.zh: 研究团队组建了「大学成果衍生企业」，以便在资助期结束后继续开发软件。

words.enDefinition: the original group of people who start and develop a venture

examples.en: The founding team met after class to agree on the first version of its service.
examples.zh: 「创始团队」课后开会，商定了第一版服务的内容。

examples.en: Two art students and a computer science student made up the founding team that term.
examples.zh: 当学期的「创始团队」由两名艺术专业学生和一名计算机专业学生组成。

words.enDefinition: an agreement setting out how business founders will work together and share rights and responsibilities

examples.en: We discussed the founder agreement with an adviser before deciding how to allocate responsibilities.
examples.zh: 在决定怎么分工前，我们和顾问讨论了「创始人协议」。

examples.en: Their founder agreement described how decisions would be made if one student left the project.
examples.zh: 他们的「创始人协议」说明了如果有学生离开项目，团队该如何作出决定。

words.enDefinition: a business co-founder who leads or contributes substantially to technical development

examples.en: The technical co-founder built the first working version while her partner organised the interviews.
examples.zh: 「技术联合创始人」做出了首个能运行的版本，她的搭档则组织访谈。

examples.en: We met a technical co-founder who had designed an app for campus bicycle repairs.
examples.zh: 我们见到一位「技术联合创始人」，他设计过一个校园自行车维修应用。

words.enDefinition: the team member who leads the exploration of a project's potential as a business

examples.en: The entrepreneurial lead organised interviews with local businesses that could use the team's design.
examples.zh: 「创业转化负责人」安排了访谈，对象是可能使用该团队设计的本地企业。

examples.en: Our entrepreneurial lead reported what customers told us during the training programme each Friday.
examples.zh: 每到周五培训时，我们的「创业转化负责人」都会汇报从客户那里听到的情况。

words.enDefinition: a session where early-stage founders bring specific problems to advisers for practical guidance

examples.en: We brought questions about the launch schedule to a venture clinic after our morning lecture.
examples.zh: 上午上完课，我们带着发布日程的问题去了「创业项目咨询活动」。

examples.en: During the venture clinic, an adviser helped us narrow our interviews to one student group.
examples.zh: 在「创业项目咨询活动」中，一位顾问帮我们把访谈范围缩小到一类学生。

collocations: bring questions to a venture clinic

words.enDefinition: an experienced person who advises a team starting or developing a venture

examples.en: The venture mentor asked whether we had spoken to students outside our immediate friendship group.
examples.zh: 「创业导师」问我们，是否找过平时关系不那么近的学生聊过。

examples.en: I met my venture mentor on Friday to discuss how to recruit pilot users.
examples.zh: 周五我见了「创业导师」，讨论怎么招募试点用户。

collocations: receive advice from a venture mentor
match a team with a venture mentor

words.enDefinition: an experienced entrepreneur affiliated with an institution to advise or work with its ventures

examples.en: The entrepreneur-in-residence held a drop-in session for teams preparing their first customer interviews that month.
examples.zh: 当月，「驻校创业导师」为准备首次客户访谈的团队办了一场无需预约的答疑。

examples.en: I asked the entrepreneur-in-residence how she had found customers when starting her first company.
examples.zh: 我问「驻校创业导师」，她开第一家公司时是怎么找到客户的。

words.enDefinition: the process of pairing participants with suitable mentors based on their needs and experience

examples.en: The programme opened mentor matching after asking each team what kind of help it needed.
examples.zh: 项目先问各团队需要哪类帮助，随后启动「导师匹配」。

examples.en: I filled in a mentor matching form before meeting an adviser from the design industry.
examples.zh: 我先填了「导师匹配」表，后来见到了一位来自设计行业的顾问。

words.enDefinition: another founder at a similar stage or in the same community

examples.en: I asked a peer founder how she scheduled interviews around classes and part-time work.
examples.zh: 我问一位「创业同辈」，她是怎么在上课和做兼职之余安排访谈的。

examples.en: A peer founder shared how his team had found a room for weekly testing.
examples.zh: 一位「创业同辈」分享了他们团队如何找到每周做测试的场地。

collocations: get advice from a peer founder

words.enDefinition: a group of founders taking part in the same programme during the same period

examples.en: Our founder cohort met every Wednesday to compare progress on interviews and early product tests.
examples.zh: 我们这个「同期创业者小组」每周三碰头，交流访谈和早期产品测试的进展。

examples.en: The new founder cohort included teams from the engineering school and the arts faculty.
examples.zh: 新的「同期创业者小组」有来自工程学院和艺术系的团队。

words.enDefinition: a programme or organisation that helps early-stage businesses develop through resources and advice

examples.en: A startup incubator gave us access to meeting rooms and an adviser for our pilot.
examples.zh: 一家「创业孵化器」让我们使用会议室，还给试点安排了一位顾问。

examples.en: My team joined a startup incubator before we had a product ready to sell.
examples.zh: 产品还没准备好上市，我们团队就加入了「创业孵化器」。

words.enDefinition: a structured, typically time-limited programme that helps startups develop and grow through intensive support

examples.en: Our startup accelerator asked each team to demonstrate progress at the end of the programme.
examples.zh: 我们的「创业加速器」要求各团队在项目结束时展示进展。

examples.en: The founders joined a startup accelerator that offered three months of workshops and mentoring.
examples.zh: 创始人加入了一个「创业加速器」，有为期三个月的工作坊和导师辅导。

words.enDefinition: a programme that helps very early teams test an idea and prepare for further development

examples.en: The pre-accelerator accepted teams that were still deciding which problem they wanted to solve.
examples.zh: 这个「预加速创业项目」也接收还在确定要解决什么问题的团队。

examples.en: We joined a pre-accelerator to check our assumptions before applying to the main programme.
examples.zh: 我们加入了「预加速创业项目」，先核实假设，再申请正式项目。

words.enDefinition: an organisation that actively builds new ventures by bringing together ideas, teams and shared resources

examples.en: The venture studio assigned two designers to help the team prepare its first prototype.
examples.zh: 「创业工作室」安排两名设计师帮助团队做出首个原型。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a venture studio that starts projects with an incubator that supports them.
examples.zh: 导师比较了自己发起项目的「创业工作室」和为项目提供支持的孵化器。

words.enDefinition: a space or programme where people collaborate and experiment with new ideas and solutions

examples.en: The innovation lab hosted a workshop on designing better signs for the campus buildings.
examples.zh: 「创新实验室」办了一个工作坊，讨论如何给校园建筑设计更好用的标识。

examples.en: We met in the innovation lab to sketch different versions of the booking screen.
examples.zh: 我们在「创新实验室」碰头，画了几个不同版本的预约界面。

words.enDefinition: individual guidance to help a person plan, start or manage a business

examples.en: The student enterprise centre offered business counselling to people preparing their first market stall.
examples.zh: 学生创业中心给第一次筹备集市摊位的人提供「经营咨询辅导」。

examples.en: I booked business counselling to discuss whether my costs made the idea realistic that term.
examples.zh: 我预约了「经营咨询辅导」，想讨论按当学期的成本算，这个想法是否现实。

words.enDefinition: a group admitted to an incubator at a particular time, or the period of admission

examples.en: The autumn incubator intake included three teams working on services for students living off campus.
examples.zh: 秋季「孵化器招收批次」有三支团队在做面向校外住宿学生的服务。

examples.en: We postponed our application until the next incubator intake to make time for interviews.
examples.zh: 我们把申请推迟到下一个「孵化器招收批次」，好腾出时间做访谈。

collocations: apply for the next incubator intake

words.enDefinition: a submission asking for a place in a business accelerator programme

examples.en: Our accelerator application explained what we had learned after six weeks of testing the idea.
examples.zh: 我们的「加速器项目申请」说明了过去六周测试创意的收获。

examples.en: I reviewed the accelerator application before my partner sent it to the programme manager.
examples.zh: 搭档把「加速器项目申请」发给项目经理之前，我又检查了一遍。

words.enDefinition: a group of people who evaluate applicants and decide who is chosen

examples.en: The selection panel asked how our service would work after the semester ended in June.
examples.zh: 「遴选评审组」问，六月学期结束后，我们的服务会怎么运行。

examples.en: We presented our prototype to a selection panel that included two former student founders.
examples.zh: 我们向「遴选评审组」展示了原型，评审中有两位曾在校创业的人。

words.enDefinition: an organised series of activities that teaches people about developing and starting a venture

examples.en: The entrepreneurship programme gave students a chance to test ideas without immediately starting a company.
examples.zh: 「创业培养项目」给了学生测试创意的机会，可以不用马上开公司。

examples.en: I joined an entrepreneurship programme that met in the business school one evening a week.
examples.zh: 我参加了一个「创业培养项目」，每周有一晚在商学院上课。

words.enDefinition: a contest in which teams prepare and present plans for new businesses

examples.en: We entered the business plan competition to get feedback on our idea for local repairs.
examples.zh: 我们参加「商业计划竞赛」，想听听大家对本地维修服务构想的意见。

examples.en: The business plan competition asked teams to explain how they would find their first customers.
examples.zh: 「商业计划竞赛」要求团队解释打算怎么找到首批客户。

words.enDefinition: a short, intensive programme that introduces people to practical aspects of starting a business

examples.en: The startup boot camp included a weekend exercise on interviewing students about everyday problems.
examples.zh: 「创业集训营」安排了一次周末练习，让大家访谈学生，了解日常遇到的问题。

examples.en: I attended a startup boot camp before deciding whether to develop the idea more seriously.
examples.zh: 我参加了一次「创业集训营」，再决定要不要更认真地做下去。

words.enDefinition: a session in which participants learn and practise how to present a venture succinctly

examples.en: The pitch workshop helped us explain what our service did without reading from the slide.
examples.zh: 「项目推介工作坊」帮我们练习不用照着幻灯片念，也能说清服务的用途。

examples.en: I brought a rough outline to the pitch workshop and tested it with another founder.
examples.zh: 我带了一份粗略提纲来参加「项目推介工作坊」，讲给另一位创业者听了听。

words.enDefinition: an event at which teams demonstrate their ventures or products to an invited audience

examples.en: We prepared three working examples for demo day at the end of the accelerator programme.
examples.zh: 加速器项目结束时有「创业项目展示日」，我们为此准备了三个能运行的演示案例。

examples.en: The audience asked about testing after our team showed the prototype on demo day.
examples.zh: 我们团队在「创业项目展示日」拿出原型后，观众问了测试情况。

words.enDefinition: a course on entrepreneurship that a student can choose as part of a programme

examples.en: My entrepreneurship elective asked us to talk to potential customers before designing a detailed solution.
examples.zh: 「创业选修课」要求我们先找潜在客户聊一聊，再详细设计解决办法。

examples.en: She took an entrepreneurship elective in her final year to learn how to test ideas.
examples.zh: 她最后一年修了「创业选修课」，学习怎样测试创意。

words.enDefinition: a way of thinking that looks for opportunities and tests practical ways to act on them

examples.en: The tutor described an entrepreneurial mindset as looking for gaps and learning through small experiments.
examples.zh: 导师把「创业者思维」解释为发现缺口，并通过小实验学习。

examples.en: The project helped students practise an entrepreneurial mindset without asking them to start a company.
examples.zh: 项目让学生练习运用「创业者思维」，无需真的开公司。

words.enDefinition: checking a set of ideas to decide which ones deserve further investigation

examples.en: We used idea screening to set aside projects that needed equipment we could not borrow.
examples.zh: 经过「创意初筛」，我们暂时放下了那些需要用到无法借到的器材的项目。

examples.en: After idea screening, our group took two options to the mentor for a longer discussion.
examples.zh: 「创意初筛」后，我们小组带着两个方案去找导师详谈。

words.enDefinition: the process of noticing a situation that could support a useful new business or service

examples.en: For our lesson on opportunity recognition, we observed how students waited for evening buses.
examples.zh: 为学习「商业机会识别」，我们观察了学生晚上怎么等公交车。

examples.en: The founder described opportunity recognition as listening for problems people encounter repeatedly on campus.
examples.zh: 那位创业者说，「商业机会识别」就是留意人们在校园里反复遇到的问题。

words.enDefinition: a situation in which a product or service could become a sustainable business

examples.en: The group saw a commercial opportunity when several societies asked about the same repair service.
examples.zh: 几个社团都问到同一种维修服务，小组看到了一个「可商业化的机会」。

examples.en: The adviser asked what made the idea a commercial opportunity beyond the one campus market.
examples.zh: 顾问问，除了这一所学校的市场之外，这个创意为什么还算一个「可商业化的机会」。

words.enDefinition: a need that existing products, services or arrangements do not adequately address

examples.en: Our interviews revealed an unmet need for equipment bookings outside the library's usual hours.
examples.zh: 访谈发现，在图书馆平时开放时间之外预约设备，是一项「未被满足的需求」。

examples.en: The team looked for an unmet need before committing to any particular design that term.
examples.zh: 当学期团队先找「未被满足的需求」，再决定要做哪种具体设计。

words.enDefinition: a problem important or frequent enough to justify spending time and resources on it

examples.en: Our adviser asked what evidence showed this was a problem worth solving for commuter students.
examples.zh: 顾问问，什么证据能说明对通勤学生来说这是个「值得解决的问题」。

examples.en: We found a problem worth solving after hearing the same concern in five separate interviews.
examples.zh: 五次单独访谈里都有人提到同一项顾虑，我们发现这是个「值得解决的问题」。

collocations: decide whether it's a problem worth solving

words.enDefinition: the way a team defines and describes a problem before working on solutions

examples.en: Changing the problem framing helped us see that students needed timely information, not another booking form.
examples.zh: 调整「界定问题的方式」让我们明白，学生需要的是及时的信息，另做一张预约表解决不了问题。

examples.en: The workshop on problem framing asked us to describe who was affected and under what circumstances.
examples.zh: 「界定问题的方式」工作坊让我们说清楚谁受到影响，以及在什么情况下受影响。

collocations: test different approaches to problem framing

words.enDefinition: learning directly from potential customers to test assumptions about their needs and behaviour

examples.en: We did customer discovery before deciding whether to develop an equipment booking service for students.
examples.zh: 我们先做「客户需求探索」，再决定要不要为学生开发设备预约服务。

examples.en: The entrepreneurship course set aside two weeks for customer discovery in nearby shops and cafés.
examples.zh: 创业课程安排了两周时间，让大家到附近的商店和咖啡馆做「客户需求探索」。

words.enDefinition: a conversation aimed at learning about someone's current problems, needs and behaviour

examples.en: In the discovery interview, I asked how the organiser currently lent equipment to new members.
examples.zh: 在「需求探索访谈」中，我问组织者，现在是怎么把器材借给新成员的。

examples.en: We changed our next discovery interview after realising we had been talking too much ourselves.
examples.zh: 我们发现自己说得太多，就调整了下一次「需求探索访谈」的做法。

collocations: record notes from a discovery interview

words.enDefinition: watching how customers behave to learn what they do in practice

examples.en: Our customer observation showed that people often skipped the instructions printed beside the rental desk.
examples.zh: 「客户行为观察」表明，人们往往不会看租赁服务台旁印着的说明。

examples.en: We used customer observation to learn where visitors stopped while trying to find our stall.
examples.zh: 我们通过「客户行为观察」了解访客找摊位时会在哪些地方停下来。

words.enDefinition: a person or organisation that might buy a product or service in the future

examples.en: I spoke to a potential customer who manages equipment for several student sports teams.
examples.zh: 我和一位「潜在客户」聊过，他管理着几支学生运动队的器材。

examples.en: A potential customer asked whether our repair service would be available over the winter break.
examples.zh: 一位「潜在客户」问，我们寒假期间有没有维修服务。

words.enDefinition: the person who actually uses a product or service, who may be different from its purchaser

examples.en: We tested the kit with an end user after speaking to the person who orders supplies.
examples.zh: 和订购耗材的人谈过之后，我们请一位「最终使用者」测试了套件。

examples.en: The end user needed to read the instructions while keeping both hands on the equipment.
examples.zh: 「最终使用者」需要在双手都放在器材上的时候读说明。

words.enDefinition: a planned list of topics or questions that helps someone conduct an interview

examples.en: I brought an interview guide but asked a few extra questions about borrowing equipment after dark.
examples.zh: 我带了「访谈提纲」，还加问了几个关于天黑以后借用器材的问题。

examples.en: Our interview guide started with questions about the student's usual journey home from evening classes.
examples.zh: 我们的「访谈提纲」先问学生平时上完晚课是怎么回家的。

words.enDefinition: an interview that encourages participants to respond in their own words rather than choosing fixed answers

examples.en: We chose an open-ended interview because we did not yet know which problems were most important.
examples.zh: 我们选了「开放式访谈」，因为还不知道哪些问题最重要。

examples.en: The open-ended interview revealed a problem that none of our survey questions had mentioned.
examples.zh: 「开放式访谈」揭示了一个我们在问卷里没有提到的问题。

words.enDefinition: a question worded without suggesting a preferred answer or implying a judgement

examples.en: The mentor asked us to start with a neutral question about how people currently book equipment.
examples.zh: 导师请我们先「中立提问」，问大家现在是怎么预约设备的。

examples.en: A neutral question gave the student room to describe what had happened in her own words.
examples.zh: 「中立提问」让那位学生能用自己的话叙述经过。

collocations: rewrite something as a neutral question

words.zhGloss: 关于问题的待验证假设
words.enDefinition: a proposed explanation of what problem particular people face or why it matters to them
acceptedZhAnswers: 关于问题的待验证假设

examples.en: Our problem hypothesis was that commuters missed repairs because the workshop closed before their classes ended.
examples.zh: 我们「关于问题的待验证假设」是：维修间在下课前就关门，通勤学生来不及过去。

examples.en: We tested the problem hypothesis by asking students to describe their last attempts to borrow equipment.
examples.zh: 我们请学生描述上一次借设备的经历，以检验「关于问题的待验证假设」。

words.enDefinition: a belief to be tested about who might use, buy or benefit from a proposed offering

examples.en: Our customer hypothesis focused on society organisers who already run several events each term.
examples.zh: 我们「关于目标客户的假设」聚焦于每学期已经办好几场活动的社团组织者。

examples.en: The interviews challenged our customer hypothesis about who would pay for a short equipment rental.
examples.zh: 访谈动摇了我们「关于目标客户的假设」，原先以为会付费短租设备的人可能不同。

words.enDefinition: a proposed idea about how a particular design or service could address an identified need

examples.en: Our solution hypothesis was that evening pickup would help students who missed the afternoon service.
examples.zh: 我们「关于解决方案的假设」是，晚间领取可以帮助赶不上下午服务的学生。

examples.en: We tested the solution hypothesis using a simple reservation form and one staffed pickup evening.
examples.zh: 我们用一张简单的预约表和一次有人员值守的晚间领取，检验了「关于解决方案的假设」。

words.enDefinition: a belief stated clearly enough that data or observation could support or challenge it

examples.en: We turned our broad claim into a testable assumption about Saturday afternoon orders from students.
examples.zh: 我们把宽泛的说法具体化，变成一个关于学生周六下午订单的「可验证的假设」。

examples.en: The project worksheet asked each team to put one testable assumption at the top of the page.
examples.zh: 项目练习表要求每支团队在页首写一个「可验证的假设」。

words.enDefinition: organising a project's assumptions so the team can decide which important uncertainties to test first

examples.en: We used assumption mapping to separate things we knew from things we still needed to test.
examples.zh: 我们通过「假设梳理与排序」，区分已经知道的情况和还需要验证的地方。

examples.en: The assumption mapping session helped the team agree on which question mattered most that week.
examples.zh: 「假设梳理与排序」的环节帮团队确定了当周最关键的问题。

words.enDefinition: an untested belief with the greatest potential to undermine a project if it is wrong

examples.en: Our riskiest assumption was that people would borrow the kits without help from a member of staff.
examples.zh: 我们「风险最高的假设」是，无需工作人员协助，人们也会来借套件。

examples.en: The mentor urged us to test our riskiest assumption before we bought any equipment for the service.
examples.zh: 导师建议，我们在为服务购买设备之前，先验证「风险最高的假设」。

words.enDefinition: information obtained directly through observation, experience or contact with the source

examples.en: We collected first-hand evidence by watching students try to check out equipment during the lunch break.
examples.zh: 我们观察学生午休时如何借设备，收集了「第一手证据」。

examples.en: The panel asked for first-hand evidence that people would use the service outside the main campus.
examples.zh: 评审组请我们提供「第一手证据」，说明主校区以外也有人会用这项服务。

words.enDefinition: comments based on individual experiences or stories rather than systematically collected data

examples.en: The survey helped us check whether the anecdotal feedback represented a wider problem with the service.
examples.zh: 问卷帮我们检查，「个别经验反馈」是否指向这项服务中更普遍的问题。

examples.en: We treated the anecdotal feedback as a starting point for another set of interviews with students.
examples.zh: 我们把「个别经验反馈」作为起点，又做了一轮学生访谈。

collocations: combine anecdotal feedback with survey data

words.enDefinition: a concise account of the main points learned in an interview

examples.en: I wrote an interview summary while the student's description of the borrowing process was still fresh.
examples.zh: 那位学生对借用流程的描述我还记得很清楚，就写了份「访谈摘要」。

examples.en: The interview summary noted that the participant had tried three different ways to find the service.
examples.zh: 「访谈摘要」记下了参与者曾试过三种方式查找这项服务。

words.enDefinition: to find and invite suitable people to take part in interviews

examples.en: We used the commuter students' newsletter to recruit interview participants from outside our own course.
examples.zh: 我们通过通勤学生通讯「招募访谈参与者」，也接触到其他专业的同学。

examples.en: Our adviser explained how to recruit interview participants without only relying on friends from class.
examples.zh: 顾问解释了怎样「招募访谈参与者」，不用只靠班里的熟人。

collocations: recruit interview participants through a notice

words.enDefinition: the match between a real customer problem and a proposed solution that addresses it

examples.en: We focused on problem-solution fit by checking whether the repair service solved a recurring problem.
examples.zh: 我们重点看「问题与方案匹配」，检查维修服务能否解决一个反复出现的问题。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for stronger evidence of problem-solution fit before we built an expensive prototype.
examples.zh: 导师要求先拿出更扎实的「问题与方案匹配」证据，再做成本高的原型。

words.enDefinition: a situation in which a product meets the needs of a market strongly enough to attract sustained demand

examples.en: Selling a few kits at one campus event did not establish product-market fit for us.
examples.zh: 在一次校园活动上只卖出了几套，这还不能说明已经做到「产品与市场匹配」。

examples.en: The mentor asked us to investigate product-market fit with customers beyond the student society.
examples.zh: 导师请我们到学生社团以外找客户，调查「产品与市场匹配」的情况。

words.enDefinition: someone who starts using a new product or service before most people do

examples.en: An early adopter used our equipment booking service every week and suggested several changes.
examples.zh: 一位「早期采用者」每周都用设备预约服务，还提了好几项修改建议。

examples.en: We asked an early adopter why she had tried the service before her friends did.
examples.zh: 我们问一位「早期采用者」，她为什么比朋友更早试用这项服务。

words.enDefinition: a user or organisation that works closely with a team to shape a product during development

examples.en: The library became a design partner and helped us test the checkout screen with students.
examples.zh: 图书馆成为「设计合作伙伴」，帮我们和学生一起测试借用界面。

examples.en: As a design partner, the cycling club offered regular feedback on each version of the repair kit.
examples.zh: 骑行社作为「设计合作伙伴」，定期对每一版维修套件提出意见。

words.enDefinition: a user who faces emerging needs ahead of most others and stands to benefit substantially from a solution

examples.en: One lead user had already built a shared spreadsheet to solve the scheduling problem herself.
examples.zh: 一位「领先用户」已经自己建了张共享表格来解决排班问题。

examples.en: We asked a lead user whether other equipment managers were beginning to face similar problems.
examples.zh: 我们问一位「领先用户」，其他器材管理员是不是也开始遇到类似问题。

words.enDefinition: a customer who uses a product or service in a limited trial before wider availability

examples.en: Our first pilot customer agreed to try the repaired bicycle service for one term.
examples.zh: 我们的首位「试点客户」同意试用翻修自行车服务一个学期。

examples.en: A pilot customer sent us comments after using the booking page for several campus events.
examples.zh: 一位「试点客户」用预约页面办过几场校园活动后，给我们发来了意见。

words.enDefinition: a planned session in which participants try using a product so the team can observe difficulties

examples.en: During the user testing session, students tried to find a pickup time without asking for help.
examples.zh: 那次「用户测试」中，同学们试着自己找到一个取件时间。

examples.en: The team recorded which step caused confusion in the user testing session on Tuesday afternoon.
examples.zh: 团队记下了周二下午那次「用户测试」中让人看不懂的步骤。

words.enDefinition: a person who takes part in a test, such as a trial of a design

examples.en: Each test participant was asked to borrow a sample kit using only the printed instructions.
examples.zh: 我们请每位「测试参与者」只看纸质说明，借一份样品套件。

examples.en: One test participant found the return button without seeing the sign at the entrance.
examples.zh: 一位「测试参与者」没看到入口的指示牌，也找到了归还按钮。

words.enDefinition: a way of addressing a problem that can realistically work under the available conditions

examples.en: Our group found a viable solution once the library agreed to handle evening collection.
examples.zh: 图书馆同意负责晚间领取后，我们小组找到了一个「切实可行的解决方案」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether this was a viable solution for a society with only two volunteers.
examples.zh: 导师问，对于只有两名志愿者的社团来说，这算不算「切实可行的解决方案」。

words.enDefinition: evidence suggesting that people are beginning to use or accept a new product or service

examples.en: We treated repeat bookings from the same society as an adoption signal rather than a guarantee.
examples.zh: 我们把同一个社团多次预约视为「开始采用的迹象」，仍继续观察后续使用。

examples.en: An adoption signal appeared when volunteers began recommending the app without being asked.
examples.zh: 志愿者开始主动推荐应用，出现了「开始采用的迹象」。

words.enDefinition: an early model of a product made so that a team can explore or test its design

examples.en: Our prototype showed how students could reserve a bicycle without visiting the repair stand first.
examples.zh: 我们的「原型」展示了学生怎样不用先去维修摊就能预约自行车。

examples.en: The team built a prototype with borrowed materials before ordering the parts it needed.
examples.zh: 团队先用借来的材料做了一个「原型」，后来才订购需要的零件。

words.enDefinition: a simple early model that shows the main ideas without looking or working like a finished product

examples.en: We used a low-fidelity prototype on paper to test the order of the booking steps.
examples.zh: 我们用纸做了一个「低保真原型」，测试预约步骤的顺序。

examples.en: The tutor encouraged us to improve the low-fidelity prototype before spending time on visual details.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们先改好「低保真原型」，再花时间打磨视觉细节。

words.enDefinition: a detailed model that resembles the intended product in appearance, interaction or behaviour

examples.en: We built a high-fidelity prototype after students could complete the main task on the mock-up.
examples.zh: 同学们能在样稿上完成主要任务后，我们做了「高保真原型」。

examples.en: The high-fidelity prototype looked like the finished service but did not handle real bookings yet.
examples.zh: 「高保真原型」看起来像最终的服务，但还处理不了真实预约。

words.enDefinition: a model that allows users to interact with simulated features or controls

examples.en: The interactive prototype let students select a pickup time and see a sample confirmation screen.
examples.zh: 学生可以在「可交互原型」上选领取时间，并看到示例确认页面。

examples.en: We shared the interactive prototype so classmates could try the buttons before the studio session.
examples.zh: 我们分享了「可交互原型」，让同学在工作室课开始前试用里面的按钮。

words.enDefinition: an early model that performs one or more of the intended practical functions

examples.en: Our functional prototype recorded returns even though its display showed only a few basic options.
examples.zh: 我们的「功能原型」虽只显示几个基本选项，却已经能记录归还。

examples.en: The team tested a functional prototype that could process real orders during the workshop trial.
examples.zh: 在工作坊试用环节，团队测试了一个能处理真实订单的「功能原型」。

words.enDefinition: a small test or demonstration showing that an idea is technically or practically feasible

examples.en: We made a proof of concept to show that the sensor could report when a shelf was empty.
examples.zh: 我们做了「概念验证」，演示传感器可以在货架空了时发出报告。

examples.en: The proof of concept worked in one room before we tried it across the building.
examples.zh: 「概念验证」先在一个房间里成功，接着我们才在整栋楼试用。

words.enDefinition: to make a model that shows how a design is intended to look or be arranged

examples.en: We decided to build a mock-up of the sign so students could comment on its layout.
examples.zh: 我们决定「制作模拟样稿」展示标牌布局，让同学们提意见。

examples.en: I used card from the studio to build a mock-up before the group discussion.
examples.zh: 小组讨论前，我用工作室的卡纸「制作模拟样稿」。

collocations: build a mock-up of a design

words.enDefinition: a model made from paper to test a design or sequence before implementing it

examples.en: The paper prototype had separate cards for the pages students would see on their phones.
examples.zh: 「纸质原型」每页用一张单独的卡片，模拟学生在手机上会看到的内容。

examples.en: We changed the order of the cards in the paper prototype after watching three people try it.
examples.zh: 看过三个人试用后，我们调换了「纸质原型」中卡片的顺序。

words.enDefinition: trying out an early model to see how it works and what might need to change

examples.en: During prototype testing, we saw several students try to return equipment before finding the confirmation screen.
examples.zh: 在「原型测试」中，我们看到几名学生没找到确认页面，就先尝试归还器材。

examples.en: We planned prototype testing for a quiet afternoon when the equipment desk was less busy.
examples.zh: 我们把「原型测试」安排在一个清闲的下午，那时器材服务台人比较少。

words.enDefinition: a cycle of revising and retesting a prototype in response to what a team learns

examples.en: Our next prototype iteration focused on making the printed instructions easier to read at a distance.
examples.zh: 下一轮「原型迭代」着重让纸质说明离远一点也能看清。

examples.en: The prototype iteration took two days because the team already knew which steps needed changing.
examples.zh: 这一轮「原型迭代」用了两天，因为团队已知道哪些步骤需要改。

words.enDefinition: the sequence of steps and experiences someone goes through while trying to achieve a goal with a service

examples.en: We mapped the user journey from finding the repair stand to collecting the finished bicycle.
examples.zh: 我们画出了从找到维修摊到取回修好自行车的「用户历程」。

examples.en: The user journey revealed that many students had to ask twice about the pickup time.
examples.zh: 「用户历程」显示，很多学生得问两遍才能确定取件时间。

words.enDefinition: an account of how a person or system uses a product to achieve a particular goal

examples.en: We wrote a use case about a volunteer lending equipment when the regular desk was closed.
examples.zh: 我们写了一个「使用场景」，描述常规服务台关闭后志愿者如何出借器材。

examples.en: The mentor asked whether the prototype addressed the most common use case during the semester.
examples.zh: 导师问，原型能不能应付学期中最常见的「使用场景」。

words.enDefinition: a basic usable version of a product built with enough features to test important assumptions with real users

examples.en: Our minimum viable product accepted reservations for just one collection point near the student centre.
examples.zh: 我们的「最小可行产品」只能预约学生中心附近的一个领取点。

examples.en: We released a minimum viable product to see whether people would use the service repeatedly.
examples.zh: 我们发布了「最小可行产品」，想看看大家会不会反复使用这项服务。

words.enDefinition: the start of a limited live trial before a product or service is offered more widely

examples.en: The pilot launch gave volunteers a chance to use the new process with real bookings.
examples.zh: 「试点启动」后，志愿者有机会把新流程用到真实预约上。

examples.en: We scheduled the pilot launch for a week when the usual equipment desk could help.
examples.zh: 我们选了常规器材服务台能帮忙的一周作为「试点启动」时间。

words.enDefinition: a trial restricted to selected people or organisations invited by its organisers

examples.en: We ran an invite-only pilot with three clubs that frequently used the same campus spaces.
examples.zh: 我们和三个经常用同一批校园场地的社团做了「仅限受邀者的试点」。

examples.en: The invite-only pilot helped us resolve scheduling problems before opening the service to other groups.
examples.zh: 「仅限受邀者的试点」帮我们解决了时间安排问题，之后才向其他小组开放服务。

words.enDefinition: the group of people or organisations selected to take part in a limited trial

examples.en: The first pilot cohort included students from three departments who often borrowed the same equipment.
examples.zh: 第一批「试点参与群体」来自三个系，他们经常借用同样的器材。

examples.en: Our pilot cohort gave feedback after trying the service for two weeks during term time.
examples.zh: 学期内试用两周后，我们的「试点参与群体」给出了反馈。

collocations: follow up with the pilot cohort

words.enDefinition: someone who tries a pre-release or beta version of a product and helps identify problems

examples.en: A beta tester reported that the booking form did not fit on a smaller phone.
examples.zh: 一位「测试版试用者」报告，预约表在小屏手机上显示不全。

examples.en: I volunteered as a beta tester because I usually borrow equipment before the library opens.
examples.zh: 我报名做「测试版试用者」，因为我经常在图书馆开门前借器材。

words.enDefinition: a beta test limited to a selected group of users

examples.en: The team ran a closed beta with two societies before inviting students from other departments.
examples.zh: 团队先请两个社团试用「封闭测试」，后来才邀请其他系的学生。

examples.en: We made changes after the closed beta showed that several labels were hard to understand.
examples.zh: 「封闭测试」反馈显示好几个标签不好懂，我们据此作了修改。

words.enDefinition: a beta test open to a wider public so more people can try the product and provide feedback

examples.en: During our open beta, students at any nearby university could try the interactive campus map.
examples.zh: 在「公开测试」期间，本地各高校的学生都能试用这张互动校园地图。

examples.en: The help page explained that search might still be unreliable during the open beta.
examples.zh: 帮助页面说明，「公开测试」期间搜索功能可能还不稳定。

words.enDefinition: a test conducted in the place or conditions where a product or service is intended for use

examples.en: We ran a field trial by letting students try the equipment station during two evening classes.
examples.zh: 我们让学生在两场晚课期间试用器材站，做了「实际环境试验」。

examples.en: The field trial showed that the printed sign was hard to see from the footpath.
examples.zh: 「实际环境试验」表明，从步道上很难看清印出来的标牌。

words.enDefinition: making a product or change available gradually while monitoring its effects

examples.en: We used a controlled rollout so the busiest societies could keep their old booking process initially.
examples.zh: 我们采用「受控分批推出」，让最忙的社团起初还能沿用旧的预约流程。

examples.en: The controlled rollout expanded after the first two departments reported that their reservations worked normally.
examples.zh: 头两个系反馈预约正常后，「受控分批推出」扩大了范围。

words.enDefinition: a limited or lightly publicised opening before a more widely announced launch

examples.en: During the soft launch, we kept the new stall open for just two afternoons.
examples.zh: 「低调试运营」期间，我们的新摊位只开了两个下午。

examples.en: The team changed its opening hours after the soft launch attracted students later than expected.
examples.zh: 「低调试运营」时，学生来的时间比预期晚，团队随后调整了开放时间。

words.enDefinition: the point when a business, product or service becomes openly available to its intended public

examples.en: We organised the public launch after the service had been tested with several student societies.
examples.zh: 服务和几个学生社团一起测试过后，我们才组织「正式公开推出」。

examples.en: The public launch included a demonstration for anyone passing through the university's central courtyard.
examples.zh: 「正式公开推出」时有一场演示，经过学校中心庭院的人都可以看。

words.enDefinition: an initial attempt made to see whether a process or arrangement works in practice

examples.en: Our trial run showed that one volunteer was not enough to check all the reservations.
examples.zh: 「试运行」表明，一名志愿者来不及核对所有预约。

examples.en: We carried out a trial run with borrowed display stands before paying for our own.
examples.zh: 自己花钱买之前，我们先借来展示架做了「试运行」。

words.enDefinition: an early development version used for initial testing, typically before the beta stage

examples.en: The alpha version could save a booking but did not yet send a confirmation message.
examples.zh: 「早期测试版」可以保存预约，但还不能发送确认消息。

examples.en: Our tutor tried the alpha version before we invited anyone outside the project to use it.
examples.zh: 我们邀请项目外的人使用之前，导师试了「早期测试版」。

words.enDefinition: a list of tasks or conditions to check before opening or releasing a product or service

examples.en: The launch checklist asked who could answer student questions during the first week of operation.
examples.zh: 「发布前检查清单」里有一项，要确认服务运行首周谁来回答学生提问。

examples.en: We added another payment test to the launch checklist after practising with fake orders.
examples.zh: 用模拟订单练习后，我们在「发布前检查清单」上又加了一个支付测试项。

words.enDefinition: how well a product, team and its supporting arrangements are prepared for a launch

examples.en: We reviewed launch readiness after volunteers tried to handle several bookings in a single hour.
examples.zh: 志愿者试着在一小时内处理几个预约后，我们评估了「发布准备程度」。

examples.en: The mentor asked what evidence of launch readiness the student team could show that afternoon.
examples.zh: 顾问问，学生团队当天下午能拿出什么证据来说明「发布准备程度」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement allowing selected users or the public to try a product before its general release

examples.en: I joined the early access programme so I could use the tool for our club's events.
examples.zh: 我参加了「提前体验计划」，这样就能在社团活动中用这个工具。

examples.en: The group started an early access programme to collect feedback before the next public release.
examples.zh: 小组启动了「提前体验计划」，准备在下一次公开发布前收集意见。

words.enDefinition: comments about how well a particular part of a product works or meets users' needs

examples.en: We collected feature feedback on the calendar rather than asking students to review the whole service.
examples.zh: 我们收集了关于日历的「对具体功能的反馈」，而没有让学生评价整个服务。

examples.en: The feature feedback helped us decide where to put the button for changing a pickup time.
examples.zh: 「对具体功能的反馈」帮我们决定了修改领取时间的按钮放在哪儿。

words.enDefinition: how much someone is prepared to pay for a product or service

examples.en: We asked about willingness to pay after hearing that several societies already borrowed equipment for free.
examples.zh: 得知好几个社团已经能免费借器材，我们接着询问了「支付意愿」。

examples.en: The pilot compared completed purchases at several prices to estimate students' willingness to pay.
examples.zh: 试点比较了几个价位的实际购买情况，以估计学生的「支付意愿」。

words.enDefinition: using the same product or service on more than one occasion

examples.en: We looked for repeat use after the excitement of the initial demonstration had died down.
examples.zh: 首场演示的新鲜劲过去后，我们观察有没有人「重复使用」。

examples.en: The booking records showed repeat use by several clubs rather than visits by new users.
examples.zh: 预约记录显示，有几个社团在「重复使用」，而没有新用户到访。

words.enDefinition: how many of the people who try a new product keep using it after their first use

examples.en: We tracked early user retention by checking who made another booking during the following month.
examples.zh: 我们查看接下来一个月谁又预约了，以跟踪「早期用户留存」。

examples.en: The mentor asked about early user retention because the first week had many one-time users.
examples.zh: 第一周很多人只用过一次，所以顾问询问了「早期用户留存」情况。

words.enDefinition: to substantially change the direction of a venture idea in response to what the team learns

examples.en: We decided to pivot the business after students asked for evening pickups rather than deliveries.
examples.zh: 学生提出想在晚上自取，我们决定「调整创业方向」。

examples.en: The mentor asked whether we could pivot the business without rebuilding the whole booking system.
examples.zh: 导师问，能不能在不用重做整套预约系统的情况下「调整创业方向」。

collocations: be ready to pivot the business

words.enDefinition: to change a working belief after receiving new information or evidence

examples.en: We had to revise an assumption about demand after speaking to students on two other campuses.
examples.zh: 和另外两个校区的学生聊过后，我们得「修正假设」，重新判断需求。

examples.en: One interview encouraged us to revise an assumption rather than restart the whole project that week.
examples.zh: 一次访谈让我们选择「修正假设」，不必当周把整个项目推倒重来。

collocations: use feedback to revise an assumption

words.enDefinition: to demonstrate that evidence contradicts a hypothesis under the tested conditions

examples.en: One unexpected result was not enough to invalidate a hypothesis about regular equipment use.
examples.zh: 一次出乎意料的结果不足以「证伪关于器材常规使用的假设」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what kind of test could invalidate a hypothesis about weekly student demand.
examples.zh: 导师问，哪种测试能「证伪关于学生每周需求的假设」。

collocations: enough evidence to invalidate a hypothesis
use data to invalidate a hypothesis

words.enDefinition: an experiment that did not produce the intended outcome or could not be completed as intended

examples.en: The team treated its failed experiment as evidence that the pickup process still needed work.
examples.zh: 团队把「失败的实验」视为一个信号，说明领取流程还有待改进。

examples.en: We wrote about the failed experiment in our report and explained why people had stopped halfway.
examples.zh: 我们在报告里写了这次「失败的实验」，也解释了为什么大家做到一半就停了。

words.enDefinition: a report describing what a team learned while testing its ideas and assumptions

examples.en: Our learning report focused on what changed after we talked to three different equipment managers.
examples.zh: 我们的「试验学习总结」重点记录，与三位器材管理员交谈后，认识有哪些变化。

examples.en: The mentor asked to see our learning report before approving another round of interviews next week.
examples.zh: 导师想先看我们的「试验学习总结」，再批准下周开展新一轮访谈。

words.enDefinition: a decision on whether to proceed with a project, release or planned activity

examples.en: We made the go/no-go decision after reviewing what had happened during the two campus trials.
examples.zh: 看过两次校园试点的结果，我们作了「继续或停止的决定」。

examples.en: The advisor postponed our go/no-go decision until the last team had reported its findings.
examples.zh: 顾问把「继续或停止的决定」推迟到最后一支团队汇报结果之后。

words.enDefinition: a meeting or assessment that checks progress at a planned point in a project

examples.en: At the milestone review, we presented test results from the library and the student centre.
examples.zh: 在「阶段成果评审」中，我们展示了图书馆和学生中心的测试结果。

examples.en: The milestone review identified two tasks the team needed to finish before inviting more users.
examples.zh: 「阶段成果评审」确定了邀请更多用户前团队得完成的两项任务。

words.enDefinition: a short presentation in which a founder explains a venture and seeks interest or support

examples.en: The founder pitch started with a real problem the team had observed at several campus events.
examples.zh: 那场「创业者项目推介」开头讲了团队在几场校园活动中观察到的一个真实问题。

examples.en: I practised my founder pitch with two classmates who had never heard of the project.
examples.zh: 我找两个没听过这个项目的同学练习「创业者项目推介」。

collocations: give feedback on a founder pitch

words.enDefinition: a very brief presentation that explains a proposal, product or venture in about a minute

examples.en: The tutor asked for a one-minute pitch before we prepared the full presentation for Friday.
examples.zh: 为周五准备完整演示前，导师让我们先做个「一分钟推介」。

examples.en: My one-minute pitch explained who used the service, what it did and why it mattered.
examples.zh: 我的「一分钟推介」说明了谁用这项服务、它能做什么，以及为什么有用。

words.enDefinition: a practice session before giving a pitch to its intended audience

examples.en: Our pitch rehearsal showed that the live demonstration took longer than we had planned.
examples.zh: 「推介演练」发现，现场演示比我们计划的用时更长。

examples.en: Two other founders attended our pitch rehearsal and questioned how we would reach more customers.
examples.zh: 另外两位创业者参加了我们的「推介演练」，问我们怎么接触到更多客户。

collocations: give feedback at a pitch rehearsal

words.enDefinition: a collection of slides used to explain and promote a business proposal or venture

examples.en: Our pitch deck used one slide to explain how students currently borrow equipment from clubs.
examples.zh: 我们的「创业推介幻灯片」用了一页说明学生目前怎么向社团借用器材。

examples.en: I shortened the pitch deck after realising we had only five minutes to present.
examples.zh: 发现介绍时间只有五分钟后，我删减了「创业推介幻灯片」。

words.enDefinition: the first part of a pitch, where the presenter introduces the main situation or attracts interest

examples.en: We changed our pitch opening to start with a story from the campus equipment desk.
examples.zh: 我们改了「推介开场」，从校园器材服务台的一段经历讲起。

examples.en: The pitch opening described a familiar problem before we showed the design on screen.
examples.zh: 「推介开场」先讲了大家熟悉的一个问题，然后才在屏幕上展示设计。

words.enDefinition: the aspects judges consider when assessing a pitch, such as evidence, feasibility or clarity

examples.en: We read the pitch judging criteria to see whether the panel expected evidence from potential customers.
examples.zh: 我们看了「推介评审标准」，想知道评审是否要求提供来自潜在客户的证据。

examples.en: The organisers explained the pitch judging criteria before anyone submitted their slides for the final round.
examples.zh: 最终一轮提交幻灯片之前，组织者解释了「推介评审标准」。

words.enDefinition: a question period during or after a pitch when the audience can ask the team for details

examples.en: During the pitch Q&A, a judge asked why our first tests involved only one sports club.
examples.zh: 在「推介问答」中，一位评审问首轮测试为什么只找了一个体育社团。

examples.en: We rehearsed the pitch Q&A with classmates who had not seen the slide deck yet.
examples.zh: 我们找了还没看过幻灯片的同学，陪我们演练「推介问答」。

collocations: answer questions in the pitch Q&A

words.enDefinition: an account of what led a founder to start a business and how it developed

examples.en: Her founder story explained how borrowing art equipment as a student led to the venture.
examples.zh: 她的「创业者经历」讲了在校时借用艺术器材的体验如何促成这次创业。

examples.en: The coach asked us to connect our founder story to the problem we had observed.
examples.zh: 教练请我们把「创业者经历」和已经观察到的问题联系起来。

collocations: include a founder story in a pitch

words.enDefinition: a slide in a pitch that shows the problem or unmet need a venture intends to address

examples.en: The problem slide showed how much time students spent finding a place to borrow tools.
examples.zh: 「问题说明页」展示了学生找地方借工具要花多少时间。

examples.en: We cut the problem slide down to one example from our interviews with society organisers.
examples.zh: 我们删减了「问题说明页」，只留了一个访谈社团组织者得到的例子。

words.enDefinition: a slide in a pitch that presents the proposed product or service as a solution

examples.en: Our solution slide illustrated how a booking appears to both the library and the student.
examples.zh: 「解决方案页」图示了同一条预约在图书馆和学生端分别是什么样。

examples.en: The team added a drawing to the solution slide so the process was easier to follow.
examples.zh: 团队在「解决方案页」加了一幅图，让流程更容易看懂。

words.enDefinition: a slide showing measurable signs that a venture is gaining users, sales or other engagement

examples.en: The traction slide showed how many clubs had booked equipment more than once that semester.
examples.zh: 「进展和市场验证页」显示，当学期有多少社团预约器材超过一次。

examples.en: We updated the traction slide after the second library began accepting bookings from our tool.
examples.zh: 第二家图书馆开始通过我们的工具接收预约后，我们更新了「进展和市场验证页」。

collocations: add evidence to the traction slide

words.enDefinition: a short recording showing how a product, service or prototype works

examples.en: We filmed a demo video so the panel could review our prototype after the presentation.
examples.zh: 我们录了「演示视频」，评审组在介绍结束后可以回看我们的原型。

examples.en: The demo video followed a student from making a booking to collecting the borrowed equipment.
examples.zh: 「演示视频」跟拍了一名学生从预约到领取借用器材的过程。

words.enDefinition: a guided explanation showing the main features or steps involved in using a product

examples.en: Our product walkthrough started with the same booking question students had raised in the survey.
examples.zh: 我们的「产品使用演示」从学生在问卷里提到的那个预约问题讲起。

examples.en: The judges followed the product walkthrough on their own screens during the final presentation session.
examples.zh: 最终展示环节，评审各自在屏幕上跟着看了「产品使用演示」。

words.enDefinition: a specific fact, figure or example used to support a broader claim

examples.en: We used the second library's signup as a proof point that the service could expand.
examples.zh: 我们用第二家图书馆的加入作为「佐证」，表明服务规模还可以扩大。

examples.en: A useful proof point came from records showing repeat orders over three months of testing.
examples.zh: 一项有用的「佐证」来自记录，三个月的测试期间有人重复下单。

words.enDefinition: a discussion after a pitch to review what happened and what could be improved

examples.en: In our post-pitch debrief, we noticed that the audience misunderstood the same example twice.
examples.zh: 在「推介后的复盘」里，我们发现观众两次都误解了同一个例子。

examples.en: Our post-pitch debrief helped us choose which feedback to use before applying to another programme.
examples.zh: 「推介后的复盘」帮我们决定，申请另一个项目前该采用哪些反馈。

collocations: take notes at a post-pitch debrief

words.enDefinition: the specific funding, partnership or other support a presenter requests from a pitch audience

examples.en: Our pitch ask was for space to run weekend tests with two student societies.
examples.zh: 我们「推介结尾的具体请求」是借用场地，周末和两个学生社团一起做测试。

examples.en: The mentor helped us make the pitch ask specific enough for the judges to act on.
examples.zh: 导师帮我们把「推介结尾的具体请求」说得更明确，方便评审提供帮助。

words.enDefinition: a short document that outlines a proposed venture and what it aims to achieve

examples.en: We submitted a venture concept note before the incubator asked us to prepare a full application.
examples.zh: 孵化器要求准备完整申请前，我们先递交了一份「创业构想简报」。

examples.en: The venture concept note explained who might use the repair service and why it was needed.
examples.zh: 「创业构想简报」说明了谁可能会用维修服务，以及为什么需要。

words.enDefinition: a plan showing the main stages and milestones in developing a venture over time

examples.en: The venture roadmap put testing ahead of expansion to the other side of the campus.
examples.zh: 「创业项目路线图」把测试排在了扩展到校园另一头之前。

examples.en: We revised the venture roadmap when another team offered to share its workshop space.
examples.zh: 另一支团队提出共享工作坊场地后，我们修改了「创业项目路线图」。

words.enDefinition: significant points used to track a new venture's progress

examples.en: The tutor asked each team to list venture milestones it could reach before the end of term.
examples.zh: 导师请各团队列出学期结束前可以达到的「创业发展里程碑」。

examples.en: Signups from two universities counted among our venture milestones during the first year of testing.
examples.zh: 测试第一年，两所大学报名加入，算是我们的「创业发展里程碑」。

words.enDefinition: a sequence of steps by which a research result or new idea can become a market offering

examples.en: The team outlined a commercialisation pathway from a laboratory demonstration to testing with local customers.
examples.zh: 团队列出了一条从实验室演示到和本地客户共同测试的「成果商业化路径」。

examples.en: We discussed which partners could help with the commercialisation pathway after the grant ended.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了资助结束后，哪些伙伴能协助推进「成果商业化路径」。

words.enDefinition: money awarded to help develop or test a new product, process or idea

examples.en: The students used an innovation grant to pay for the materials needed for their test.
examples.zh: 同学们用「创新项目资助」支付了测试所需的材料费用。

examples.en: Our tutor read the innovation grant application and suggested making the experiment more specific.
examples.zh: 导师看了「创新项目资助」申请，建议把实验写得更具体。

collocations: fund a pilot with an innovation grant

words.enDefinition: a grant that provides a small amount of money for a specific project or activity

examples.en: A microgrant covered the first set of materials for our student-run repair stall that month.
examples.zh: 当月，一笔「小额资助」支付了学生经营的维修摊所需的第一批材料。

examples.en: The programme awarded a microgrant after the team explained how it planned to test the idea.
examples.zh: 团队讲清怎样测试创意之后，项目方发放了一笔「小额资助」。

words.enDefinition: a fixed payment that supports someone taking part in a programme, placement or study

examples.en: The participant stipend helped cover my travel to the entrepreneurship programme during the spring term.
examples.zh: 春季学期，「参与津贴」帮我负担了参加创业培养项目的交通费。

examples.en: The application explained how and when students would receive their participant stipend after joining.
examples.zh: 申请材料说明了学生加入后如何、何时领取「参与津贴」。

words.enDefinition: a former student of an institution who has founded a company or venture

examples.en: An alumni founder returned to campus to discuss her first year of running a business.
examples.zh: 一位「校友创业者」回到学校，谈自己经营公司的第一年。

examples.en: We met an alumni founder who had started a small studio while completing his degree.
examples.zh: 我们见了一位「校友创业者」，他在读学位时创办了一个小工作室。
